US Senate Russia-Iran sanctions deal, 28 July 2026:

A bipartisan group of senators announced a deal Tuesday (28 July) on the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia Act of 2026 (S. 5025). More than 60 bipartisan co-sponsors; has cleared the 60-vote threshold needed to defeat a filibuster.

Provisions: Would authorise the president to impose up to 100% tariffs on the five largest buyers of Russian crude oil and natural gas — including China and India — as well as on five countries that most actively help Russia circumvent energy sanctions.

Iran: The bill also extends the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996 through 2031, preserving US authority to impose secondary sanctions on non-American companies doing business with Iran (the act was due to expire this year).

Vote: A procedural vote was scheduled for the evening of 28 July (late Tuesday, US time). Trump signalled support. Some Democrats opposed, warning Trump could use the tariff authority as legal justification for broad new tariffs.
NOTE: As of ~18:40 BST / 13:40 EDT 28 July, the procedural vote had not yet occurred — result unconfirmed.
